Consider a client that manages its cart items via the Web App and an administrator who manages the catalog via the REST API.

The flow of requests is illustrated in a shared [figure](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tvxXGYsScQAVJruN8ydk3aSRd-IpnS0r/view?usp=sharing). rows.title: Catalog API admin mutation endpoints have no authentication - unauthenticated item creation, update, and deletion
rows.excerpt:
### Summary

The Catalog API registers CreateItem, UpdateItem (v1 and v2), and DeleteItemById endpoints with no authentication or authorization requirement. Any unauthenticated network client can create, overwrite, or delete catalog items. Unlike every other microservice in the application (Ordering, Basket, Webhooks), the Catalog API does not call `builder.AddDefaultAuthentication()` in its Extensions.cs and does not apply `.RequireAuthorization()` to its mutation routes.

### Details

In `src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs` (lines 92-110), the mutation routes are registered as:

```csharp
v1.MapPut("/items", UpdateItemV1)
v2.MapPut("/items/{id:int}", UpdateItem)
api.MapPost("/items", CreateItem)
api.MapDelete("/items/{id:int}", DeleteItemById)
```

None of these route registrations call `.RequireAuthorization()`.

In `src/Catalog.API/Program.cs`, neither `app.UseAuthentication()` nor `app.UseAuthorization()` is called, and there is no global authorization middleware.

In `src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs`, the `AddApplicationServices` method does not call `builder.AddDefaultAuthentication()`, unlike the Basket API (`src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs` line 10: `builder.AddDefaultAuthentication()`), the Ordering API (`src/Ordering.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs` line 10: `builder.AddDefaultAuthentication()`), and the Webhooks API.

This is confirmed in the AppHost configuration (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs`): the `catalogApi` resource is the only service not passed `Identity__Url` as an environment variable. The basket, ordering, and webhooks services all receive `.WithEnvironment("Identity__Url", identityEndpoint)`, which is what triggers the JWT bearer middleware registration. Catalog receives no such configuration.

Additionally, `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs` registers a YARP catch-all route `/api/catalog/{*any}` in `ConfigureMobileBffRoutes` that forwards all catalog API requests (including mutations) from the mobile BFF without adding any authentication layer.

(available upon request)

### Impact

Any unauthenticated attacker with network access to the Catalog API (directly or via the YARP mobile BFF) can add fraudulent products at arbitrary prices, modify existing product prices to cause financial loss, or delete all catalog items to cause a denial of service for the storefront. Extract ICatalogRepository from Catalog.API to enable in-memory persistence swaps, add Serilog logging to ServiceDefaults, fix integration event type discovery under WebApplicationFactory, and add runsettings plus xUnit traits for filtering tests by mode.

# eShop Multi-Mode Functional Testing

> Architecture and design reference for eShop's pluggable functional test infrastructure,
> covering test modes, messaging validation, and related production changes.

---

## Overview

eShop functional tests use a **pluggable test-mode architecture** shared across Catalog and Ordering microservices. The main themes are:

1. **Multi-mode test infrastructure** (Aspire, mocks, in-memory EF, Testcontainers)
2. **Messaging/outbox integration tests** (RabbitMQ + transactional outbox)
3. **Catalog API repository extraction** (to enable swappable persistence in tests)
4. **Structured logging** (Serilog in production + rich test logging)
5. **Integration event discovery fix** (works under test host)

---

## Feature 1: Multi-Mode Functional Test Framework

### What Changed

The old pattern — one `WebApplicationFactory` fixture hard-wired to Aspire + PostgreSQL — was replaced with a **pluggable test-mode architecture** shared across Catalog and Ordering.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Single `CatalogApiFixture` / `OrderingApiFixture` at project root | Mode-aware fixtures under `Fixture/` |
| Always Aspire + Docker | 4–6 modes per service |
| `IClassFixture<...>` per test class | `CatalogApiTestSession` / `OrderingApiTestSession` as assembly fixture |
| Hard-coded DB assertions | Persistence helpers that work per mode |

rows.title: Reserve catalog stock when an order is validated
rows.excerpt:
## Problem
#732 
#888 
When the Catalog handles `OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEvent` it only reads `AvailableStock` and compares it to the ordered units. The stock is removed later, when `OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent` arrives. Between those two points nothing holds the stock, so several orders for the same last units can all be confirmed and paid. The later ones then hit `RemoveStock`, which either throws on empty stock or silently removes fewer units than were ordered.

## Change

- **Validation** now checks and decrements stock in a single conditional `UPDATE` per item (`WHERE AvailableStock >= units`), so the database decides who gets the last units. It is all or nothing per order: if one item is short, the decrements for the other items are rolled back and the order is rejected.
- **New `StockReservation` table** (migration `AddStockReservation`), one row per order with a status (reserved, committed, released) and the items held. The primary key on `OrderId` keeps a redelivered event from taking stock twice.
- **Cancellation**: the Catalog now subscribes to `OrderStatusChangedToCancelledIntegrationEvent` and returns the reserved stock once. This also covers payment failure, since Ordering cancels the order in that case.
- **Paid** only marks the reservation as committed. Orders validated before this change have no reservation, so their stock is still removed at payment as before.
- The stock change, the reservation and the outgoing confirm/reject event are saved in one local transaction.

## Behaviour changes

- An order containing a product id that does not exist is now rejected. Previously that item was skipped and the order confirmed.
- Available stock drops when the order is validated rather than when it is paid.
- An order cancelled before its validation event is handled leaves a released marker, so the late validation reserves nothing and publishes nothing.

## Not addressed

- Reservations do not expire. An order stuck between validation and payment holds its stock until it is paid or cancelled.
- The RabbitMQ event bus acks a message even when its handler throws, so a failed cancellation is not retried and its stock stays reserved.
- `CatalogItem.RemoveStock` no longer has callers (`AddStock` already had none). Both are left in place.

rows.title: Treat a login cookie with an expired access token as logged out
rows.excerpt:
not "fixes".

## Change

`OnValidatePrincipal` on the cookie now rejects the principal and signs out when the `expires_at` token stored in the cookie is in the past. The user is then treated as logged out and asked to log in again.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed by running Identity, Basket, Catalog, Ordering and the WebApp locally and driving the site with Playwright. To avoid waiting 2 hours, I temporarily set the `webapp` client's `AccessTokenLifetime` to 10 seconds (not part of this PR), logged in as `alice`, waited past the token's expiry plus the API's 5 minute clock skew, then added an item to the cart.

| | Item page shows | Add to cart |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | "Add to shopping bag" | POST `/item/1` returns **500**, `Unauthenticated` in the WebApp and Basket API logs |
| This PR | "Log in to purchase" | Redirected to the Identity login page, no `Unauthenticated` in the logs |

The existing Playwright suite (browse, cart, checkout) passes with the normal 2 hour lifetime.

## Not covered

- No automated test: the failure needs an access token to expire, and `Application.UnitTests` has no reference to the WebApp. I can add one if you prefer to expose the handler for testing.
- A token that the API rejects for another reason while still unexpired (for example after Identity restarts with a new signing key) is not handled by this change.

rows.title: Fix KeyNotFoundException and NullReferenceException when catalog items are deleted
rows.excerpt:
When catalog items are deleted, basket items and orders retain references to non-existent product IDs, causing the WebApp to crash with `KeyNotFoundException` during basket operations and the Catalog API to crash with `NullReferenceException` during order validation.

## Changes

**BasketState.cs**
- Replace dictionary indexer with `TryGetValue()` to handle missing catalog items
- Filter out basket items for deleted products instead of crashing
- Add warning log when skipping items

**OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEventHandler.cs**
- Handle null catalog items during order validation
- Treat deleted products as out of stock to reject orders gracefully
- Add warning log for missing products

## Example

Before:
```csharp
var catalogItem = catalogItems[item.ProductId]; // throws KeyNotFoundException
```

After:
```csharp
if (!catalogItems.TryGetValue(item.ProductId, out var catalogItem))
{
    logger.LogWarning("Basket item with ProductId {ProductId} not found in catalog and will be skipped", item.ProductId);
    continue;
}
```

This defensive approach allows the system to continue functioning when data inconsistencies occur across microservices, avoiding the need for distributed transaction coordination.
